articles.title: Palace confident China's statement would not affect ASEAN meeting in November
articles.summary: Malacañang expressed confidence Tuesday that China's recent statement would not affect the attendance of leaders of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) at the upcoming summit in the…

blocks.text: Published November 3, 2026 1:23pm

Malacañang expressed confidence Tuesday that China's recent statement would not affect the attendance of leaders of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) at the upcoming summit in the Philippines in November.

“Nakikipag-ugnayan po ang bansang Pilipinas sa lahat ng miyembro ng ASEAN at sa ibang bansa na maaaring makilahok dito sa ASEAN Summit. So, mararamdaman naman ng ibang mga liderato kung paano ba nakikipag-ugnayan ang ating bansa sa kanila,” Palace Press Officer Undersecretary Claire Castro said at a press briefing.
(The Philippines has been coordinating with members of the ASEAN and other countries in relation to the ASEAN Summit. So, the leaders know the efforts of the Philippines.)
“So sa ating pagkakaalam ay hindi naman ito maaapektuhan sa darating na ASEAN Summit,” she added.
(As far as we know, this will not be affected by the upcoming ASEAN Summit.)

Zhang Xiaogang, China’s spokesperson for the Ministry of National Defense, earlier accused the Philippines of undermining ASEAN’s spirit of openness and China’s legitimate rights as a dialogue partner.

During the ASEAN Defense Ministers’ Meeting-Plus (ADMM-Plus), Department of National Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr. welcomed defense ministers and representatives of other countries as they entered the venue, except China’s defense attaché to the Philippines Senior Captain Yang Lei.
China’s ASEAN attendance
For Castro, it is better if Chinese President Xi Jinping attends the ASEAN Summit to discuss pressing matters between neighboring countries.

“Mas maganda po na dumating po talaga ang liderato ng China dahil mas magandang pagkakataon ito para mapag-usapan kung ano man yung maaaring may gusot at doon magkaroon na pagkakataong maresolba,” Castro said.
(It is better if Xi Jinping attends the ASEAN Summit because it is a good opportunity for state leaders to talk about pressing issues and to solve them.)
“Kasi kaya nga po ito summit, para kung ano man yung mga issues among the region ay mapag-usapan at maayos,” she added.
(That's what this summit is for. Whatever issues there are among the region can be discussed and resolved.)
When asked if Marcos invited Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping to attend the ASEAN Summit, Castro said further details will be shared once she acquires it from the Department of Foreign Affairs.
To recall, during his state visit to China in January in 2023, President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. invited Xi Jinping to visit the Philippines.
Marcos had a bilateral meeting with Xi at the Great Hall of the People where part of their talks focused on the West Philippine Sea. — RSJ, GMA News

articles.title: MPs granting powerful political lobbyists unfettered access to Australia’s parliament, data reveals
articles.summary:
Labor and Coalition members sponsoring resource companies and lobby group representing online gambling giants

  • Get our

blocks.text: Labor and Coalition MPs are facilitating permanent access to Parliament House for the country’s biggest resources companies and the lobby group representing online gambling giants, new data has revealed.

Updated rules about access passes to parliament’s private offices require MPs who sponsor lobbyists and other private interests to be disclosed on a public register. However, Tuesday’s first release of data provided very limited detail, with a backlog of more than 1,000 applications yet to be processed.

Woodside Energy, Australia’s largest fossil fuel company, has three access cards, sponsored by Labor politicians Meryl Swanson, Glenn Sterle and Tracey Roberts, as well as Coalition MPs Melissa Price, Rick Wilson and Susan McDonald.
Lobby group the Minerals Council of Australia also has passes sponsored by McDonald, as well as Coalition frontbenchers Angie Bell, Matt O’Sullivan and Ted O’Brien, and Labor’s Dan Repacholi.

American oil and gas giant ConocoPhillips has access sponsored by Nationals MP Colin Boyce and Labor’s Mike Freelander, while gas lobby group Australian Energy Producers is sponsored by the member for Bean, David Smith.
The shadow energy minister, Dan Tehan, sponsors access for Alinta Energy, along with Repaholi.

blocks.caption: The Labor member for Hunter, Dan Repacholi, sponsors access for lobby groups Minerals Council of Australia, the Pharmacy Guild and Alinta Energy.  Photograph: Lukas Coch/AAP

blocks.text: The shadow health minister, Anne Ruston, and Labor’s Raff Ciccone are primary sponsor for two passes for lobby group Responsible Wagering Australia, which represents betting giants bet365, Sportsbet and Betfair.

Kai Cantwell, the group’s chief lobbyist, is a former staffer to Ruston when she was a minister in the Morrison government. He was a key witness in an inquiry considering Labor’s legislation to curb gambling advertising earlier this year.

Under the new rules, two MPs are required to sponsor lobbyists to register for a pass. Until now, there has been no transparency about the more than 2,000 pass holders with access to the building, which has led to frustrations among MPs including ACT independent David Pocock.

A review of the policies governing access to the building’s private areas was conducted by the House speaker, Milton Dick, and the Senate president, Sue Lines. In March, the prime minister, Anthony Albanese, suggested greater “transparency and rigour” of sponsored pass holders was needed.
Prominent lobbyist Ben Oquist, a former Greens staffer and the husband of Greens senator Sarah Hanson-Young, is sponsored by the energy minister, Chris Bowen, and the industry minister, Tim Ayres.
Greens leader David Shoebridge sponsors access for the Australian Peace and Security Forum, a registered non-profit which is helping lead a public inquiry into the Aukus defence pact.
Pocock sponsors passes for the Australian Construction Industry Forum, Bees and Blossoms, Queensland University of Technology and Chanel Contos’s Teach Us Consent Global organisation.
Powerful lobby group the Pharmacy Guild has two sponsored passes, signed by Labor’s Gordon Reid, Anne Urquhart, Repacholi and Josh Dolega.

Transparency campaigners the Australian Democracy Network said as many as 80% of registered lobbyists are still not on the register. It has highlighted problems with the existing lobbyists register, a separate transparency tool administered by the Attorney-General’s Department.
“Unfortunately today’s partial disclosure only covers about 10% of total existing passes, meaning Australians still can’t see the full picture,” spokesman Christian Slattery said.
“The new transparency system doesn’t give meaningful information to the public about who our elected representatives are meeting with, when they’re meeting them, or why.”
He called for new national laws to cover lobbying conduct and establish a regulator.

Journalists working in Parliament House are required to apply for an access pass with support from a bureau chief or editor, and endorsed by representatives of the Federal Parliamentary Press Gallery Committee.

blocks.text: SHARIFF AGUAK, Maguindanao del Sur — The Army’s 601st Infantry Brigade has honored the 75th Infantry Battalion (75IB) for its service and contributions to maintaining peace and security in the Bangsamoro region, particularly during the first parliamentary elections on Sept. 14, 2026.

Brig. Gen. Gremel Brual, commander of the 601st Infantry Brigade, led the tribute and send-off ceremony for the battalion on Nov. 2 at the Old Capitol in Barangay Poblacion, Shariff Aguak, Maguindanao del Sur.
The Army’s 75th IB is based in Surigao del Sur and under the 401st Infantry Brigade of the 4th Infantry “Diamond” Division.
The ceremony recognized the service, dedication, and significant contributions of the 75IB under the leadership of battalion commander Lt. Col. Earl Pardillo.

In coordination with the Army’s 1st Mechanized Infantry Battalion of the Armor Division, the battalion played an important role in ensuring the orderly, peaceful conduct of the first Bangsamoro parliamentary elections in Maguindanao del Sur.
The 75IB received a plaque of recognition and medals in acknowledgment of its performance, discipline and commitment to duty.
Brual thanked the officers and battalion personnel for their professionalism and dedication.
“The 75IB contributed significantly to the peaceful conduct of the first Bangsamoro parliamentary elections and the formal inaugural session of the elected BARMM Parliament,” Brual said.
He stressed that the battalion’s departure would not diminish its contributions, which had helped establish a strong foundation for more stable, improved communities in the areas it served.

Brual added that the 601st Infantry Brigade would continue delivering services to the Bangsamoro people in partnership with local government units and community members to promote peace, order, and security in Maguindanao del Sur./coa

articles.title: JV Ejercito: Nov. 3 budget meeting to tackle bicam schedule, not realignment
articles.summary: The Nov. 3 meeting on the proposed 2027 national budget will focus on coordination and scheduling rather than the alleged realignment of funds, Senate finance committee chairperson JV Ejercito said…

blocks.text: Published November 3, 2026 12:29pm

The Nov. 3 meeting on the proposed 2027 national budget will focus on coordination and scheduling rather than the alleged realignment of funds, Senate finance committee chairperson JV Ejercito said Tuesday.

According to a report by Nimfa Ravelo on Super Radyo dzBB, Ejercito clarified that Tuesday's meeting would cover coordination, the schedule and parameters of the bicameral conference committee meetings, which will be attended by representatives of the Senate and the House of Representatives.
Ejercito earlier said the proposed 2027 budget would be reviewed and finalized in the second or third week of December to allow President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. to sign it before the end of 2026.

The senator also said he would meet with House appropriations panel senior vice chairperson Albert Garcia of Bataan, as the panel's chairperson, Nueva Ecija Rep. Mikaela Suansing, recently gave birth.
Ejercito earlier questioned the reported realignment of around P206 billion in the House of Representatives' version of the proposed P7.2-trillion national budget for 2027.
The Senate finance committee chairperson noted that allocations for some agencies had increased, including those for the Department of Agriculture and the Department of Public Works and Highways.

The meeting on the proposed 2027 national budget comes amid close scrutiny from civil society groups and budget watchdogs over red flags they have identified in the House-approved version, including the reported P206-billion realignment.
They are also closely watching what adjustments or corrections will be made when the House and Senate convene as a bicameral conference committee.— Mariel Celine Serquiña/MCG, GMA News

articles.title: Ombudsman files charges vs 6 DPWH personnel over alleged P491.9-M right-of-way 'scam'
articles.summary: The Office of the Ombudsman has filed graft and malversation charges against six Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) officials at the Sandiganbayan over their alleged involvement in a…

blocks.text: Published November 3, 2026 12:20pm

The Office of the Ombudsman has filed graft and malversation charges against six Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) officials at the Sandiganbayan over their alleged involvement in a P491.9 million “Road Right of Way Scam.”

"The office found prima facie evidence with reasonable certainty of conviction against former DPWH Region XII Regional Director Subair Saro Diron, former Assistant Regional Director Laureano B. Suan Jr., and four other DPWH personnel," the Ombudsman said in a statement.
Apart from the six DPWH officials, seven private officials were also alleged to be part of the scheme and have been included in the cases.

The Office of the Ombudsman said that it has filed 18 informations for malversation of public funds through falsification of public documents under Articles 217 and 171 of the Revised Penal Code, and another 18 informations of violating Republic Act No. 3019, or the Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act.

The Ombudsman said that the charges stemmed from three investigation reports submitted by the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) in 2018 and 2019, which involved the payment of right of way for 18 parcels of land which were allegedly affected by the construction of the Digos-Makar National Road in Lagao, General Santos City.
Witness Roberto S. Catapang Jr. said in an affidavit from 2017 that he was involved in the alleged syndicate.

“The group… in collusion with respondent public officers, collected money from the government purportedly as payments for the acquisitions, by fabricating and submitting fake documents,” Catapang said in a statement from the Ombudsman.
The Ombudsman said that the DPWH Region XII technical working group (TWG) approved the disbursement of P491,931,120.20 to claimants that were alleged to have presented falsified documents.

Aside from this, there were also inflated right-of-way claims after an allegedly unlawful use of a 2009 appraisal value of P3,500 per square meter to determine the compensation for properties taken by the government during the 1990s, investigators found. —VAL, GMA News

articles.title: PDP-Laban submits letter urging SC to resolve Duterte, Dela Rosa petitions
articles.summary: Political party Partido Demokratiko Pilipino-Lakas ng Bayan (PDP-Laban) on Tuesday submitted its open letter to the Supreme Court urging magistrates to resolve pending petitions on the arrest…

blocks.text: Published November 3, 2026 12:09pm

Political party Partido Demokratiko Pilipino-Lakas ng Bayan (PDP-Laban) on Tuesday submitted its open letter to the Supreme Court urging magistrates to resolve pending petitions on the arrest warrants against former president Rodrigo Duterte and Senator Ronald "Bato" dela Rosa in connection with their case at the International Criminal Court (ICC).

According to a report by Manny Vargas on Super Radyo dzBB, PDP-Laban spokesperson Atty. Ferdinand Topacio said they filed the open letter to the SC to respectfully present their position and urge the court to act on the pending petitions.
Signed by PDP-Laban acting chairman Alfonso Cusi, the party asserted in its open letter that prolonged delays in coming to a decision could further fuel uncertainty and instability.
PDP-Laban noted that a habeas corpus petition filed on behalf of Duterte had remained pending before the high tribunal for nearly 600 days.
It also called for the immediate resolution of Dela Rosa's pending motion for reconsideration.
The PDP-Laban, as a "concerned third party," said it would respect and abide with whatever decision the court would hand down, and that it only asks that the tribunal make a ruling.
On March 13, 2025, the Supreme Court ordered respondents to show cause within a non-extendable 24-hour period.
Members of PDP-Laban and Duterte supporters also staged Tuesday a protest action at the Supreme Court in Manila City, calling on the high tribunal to rule on petitions.
Protesters urged the Supreme Court to rule on the legality of the arrest warrants issued by the ICC regarding Duterte's crimes against humanity case.
A phalanx of policemen guarded the perimeter of the Supreme Court premises as the protesters chanted and raised placards bearing messages that justice delayed is justice denied.
Duterte was arrested by Philippine authorities in Pasay City and was handed over to the International Criminal Court (ICC) on March 11, 2025.

He was flown via a chartered plane to The Hague, where he will be tried for crimes against humanity in relation to his bloody war on drugs while he was mayor of Davao City and President of the Philippines.
The trial is scheduled to begin on November 30, 2026.
Dela Rosa is also wanted by the ICC as he is accused of being a co-perpetrator in the alleged crimes. He has not been seen in public since March.
A P50-million reward is being offered for information that would lead to the senator's arrest. — VDV, GMA News

articles.title: Australia rushed through ‘ill-thought-out’ under-16s social media ban, Reddit argues as high court challenge begins
articles.summary:
Reddit challenges ban on grounds it impinges implied freedom of political communications for teens

The Australian government’s rush to pass the

blocks.text: The Australian government’s rush to pass the under-16s social media ban legislation in 2024 led to “ill-thought-out, over-broad legislation” that has since been narrowed after Reddit sued the government, lawyers for the social media company told the high court on Tuesday.
Reddit, one of the top 10 websites visited in the world, has challenged the teen social media ban on the grounds that it impinges the implied freedom of political communication for under-16s.

In oral arguments before the high court on Tuesday, Reddit’s counsel, Perry Herzfeld SC, argued in the years leading up to the ban legislation, a 2021 parliamentary inquiry on social media had not recommended introducing a ban, with the eSafety commissioner warning the inquiry at the time it would be a “blunt force approach”.
When the government announced the ban in 2024, Reddit argued the legislation was introduced and passed within a week, with only 24 hours of submissions allowed.
“A process of this kind is likely to lead to ill-thought-out, over-broad legislation,” Herzfeld argued.

After eSafety announced Reddit would be included in the ban, and Reddit did not accept it met the definition of a social media platform under the law, the company announced the high court challenge to the law in late 2025.

In March this year, the communications minister, Anika Wells, introduced new rules as part of the legislation that defines additional requirements for social media companies to meet the definition including logged-in features, recommendation features, or endless scroll.

Herzfeld argued that the ban does not address those factors specifically by a broad ban on under-16s accounts, and has argued it would be able to under different legislation – pointing to the digital duty of care legislation currently before the parliament.
Outside the court, Wells told reporters that she wasn’t the minister at the time the legislation passed, but said the government’s arguments in response would be made in court.

Since the ban came into effect in December last year, more than 5 million user accounts across 10 platforms that those platforms believe to belong to people aged under 16 have been suspended or deactivated.
The platforms covered by the ban currently include Snapchat, TikTok, YouTube, Facebook, Instagram, Reddit, Kick, X, Twitch and Threads.

The case centres around whether the effect of the ban limiting political communications is justified by what the government has said is a “credible risk” of harms such as mental health issues, sleeping issues, and eating disorder issues among others.

Herzfeld told the court on Tuesday the burden on teens of the ban is limitations to actively engage in political communications through subreddits such as r/Australia. While they can still view the content without an account, they can’t make their own posts, comment, or upvote content, Reddit argued.

Justice Jacqueline Gleeson expressed reservations when pointed to examples of high-profile teens being politically engaged in social media – such as 6News’ Leo Puglisi, who began his news site at the age of 11.
Gleeson said the “vast majority of teens the vast majority of time” when under 16 do not engage in politics.

When asked whether teens were being limited in engaging in political communication on just those platforms covered by the ban, Herzfeld argued that the platforms offer teens a much wider audience compared with “shouting on the street” or being interviewed in the media.

The Digital Freedom Project, led by NSW Libertarian MP John Ruddick, will also be heard challenging the case this week. Ruddick was joined outside the court this morning by the original plaintiff for the case – 16-year-old Noah Jones – and his mother, Renee, as well as One Nation senator Malcolm Roberts.
The case continues.

articles.title: [Vantage Point] The bank Ginbee Go will inherit
articles.summary: Go’s tenure will be judged on whether the bank’s high-margin expansion delivered lasting enterprise value or merely postponed a reckoning with bad debt

blocks.text: On April 26, 2027, Maria Cristina “Ginbee” Go will take charge of a franchise that is both distinctly modernized and in the middle of absorbing the costs of its own rapid ambition.

She will take the helm of the Bank of the Philippine Islands (BPI) from outgoing president Jose Teodoro “TG” Limcaoco, who will leave behind an institution commanding P3.9 trillion in assets, P3 trillion in deposits, and a record P48.9 billion in nine-month net income.
During Limcaoco’s tenure, heavy capital outlays went directly into digital distribution channels, modern core architecture, and an expanding agency banking footprint.

Go is no outsider stepping into the unknown. As head of consumer banking, she helped build the very retail push she will now oversee as president, while Limcaoco remains on the board. But this transition will not be judged by loan volume alone; the real test is how much of that high-yield expansion survives the discipline of collection.
The underlying operating engine has encountered clear friction. While top-line revenue expanded 9.8% across the first nine months, operating expenses rose at a faster clip of 12.5%.

Far more telling was the credit cost: cumulative provisions surged 69.2% to P19.9 billion. A bank booking brisk retail lending while ramping up set-asides by tens of billions inevitably raises questions among investors about whether management is merely exercising prudent foresight or scrambling to erect buffers against visible borrower distress.

A closer look at the credit ledger shows an uneven landscape across business lines. The non-performing loan (NPL) ratio for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) climbed to 15.62% in September, jumping more than three percentage points in a single quarter.

Credit card delinquencies edged up to 5.44%, residential mortgages to 4.80%, and auto loans to 4.73%. By contrast, non-performing loans in personal lending retreated to 6.99%, microfinance eased to 13.95%, and institutional exposures stayed pristine at 0.86%.

Because SME credit makes up only a modest slice of the broader balance sheet, its immediate systemic drag is contained. The deeper danger lies in the process: if underwriting flaws or weak collection models are permitted to take root, expanding those loan books will only compound future losses.

Management has sought to assure the market that credit filters have tightened. Limcaoco attributed the strain in small business lending to retail and construction borrowers hit by lags in government disbursements.

Go pointed to aggressive collection campaigns, restructured facilities, and balance write-offs to explain the lower delinquency rates in microfinance and personal credit. But reported improvements in delinquency ratios carry weight only when borrowers resume regular cash payments.

A write-off cleans a ledger without clawing back lost capital, just as loan restructuring can buy time without revitalizing a borrower’s ability to pay. Until the bank discloses the actual cash recovered alongside the volume of debts rewritten or struck off, it remains difficult to verify whether these fixes represent real balance sheet rehabilitation or optical adjustments.

Recent quarterly earnings highlight this delicate balance. Net income for the period nudged up to P16.07 billion from P15.91 billion, but the gain owed its momentum to a decline in quarterly provisions, which fell to P6.54 billion from P7.84 billion.
Operating performance beneath the surface looked softer: pre-provision operating profit slipped to P27.23 billion from P27.96 billion, and net interest margins compressed from 4.70% to 4.56%.
A rising bottom line built on curtailed provisioning, against a backdrop of shrinking core margins, cannot easily be mistaken for accelerating business momentum.

The mechanics behind the bank’s provisioning models demand equal scrutiny. Management kept its June macroeconomic assumptions in place through September, carrying a year-to-date expected-credit-loss overlay of P2.7 billion.

Staging adjustments were attributed to regulatory feedback from the central bank suggesting certain loans had been shifted prematurely into Stage 3 rather than Stage 2. This remains management’s characterization, and holding broader economic inputs steady does not answer how provisions should evolve as individual credit exposures deteriorate.

Reserve adequacy presents its own puzzles. BPI reports an accounting NPL coverage ratio of 89.57%, which widens to 113.05% under regulatory formulas. While sub-100% accounting coverage is not inherently dangerous when loans are backstopped by solid collateral, the bank’s own investor disclosures contain oddities.

In the personal loan book, reported “total cover” appears lower than the reserve coverage itself, despite being defined as the sum of reserves and pledged collateral. Clarifying that anomaly is an immediate disclosure priority.
To gauge how sensitive BPI’s bottom line is to unexpected credit deterioration, consider an incremental provisioning shock of 1% across the rounded P2.7 trillion loan book.

That single percentage point would generate a pre-tax charge of P27 billion. Even after factoring in a 25% tax shield, the resulting P20.25 billion hit would erase roughly 41% of the bank’s nine-month profit.
This arithmetic is an indicator of earnings vulnerability rather than a forecast of imminent ruin, especially with common equity Tier 1 sitting at 13.9% and total capital adequacy at 14.7%.

Still, earlier first-half marks revealed P13.44 billion in fair-value losses on debt securities taken directly through equity, alongside a P5.53 billion unbooked fair-value shortfall on amortized-cost paper that awaits updated September transparency.

Financing decisions will add another layer of complexity to Go’s tenure. The planned P5 billion SIBOL or Sustainable Impact Building Our Legacy — BPI’s name for its proposed P5 billion sustainability bond offering — issue brings in wholesale borrowed funds rather than equity capital.
Meanwhile, the bank’s role in Citicore’s roughly P35 billion syndicated solar facility requires careful monitoring of retained credit risk, actual funding drawdowns, and project repayment terms.
Limcaoco still has several months to fortify the foundation before the formal handover. He leaves his successor an enviable retail network, deep funding pools, and scale.
But Go’s tenure will be judged on whether the bank’s high-margin expansion delivered lasting enterprise value or merely postponed a reckoning with bad debt.
The coming years will prove whether today’s balance sheet growth can truly be converted into durable cash.

(This is to be continued in my next newsletter. My analysis draws from BPI’s October 21, 2026 leadership and earnings announcements, its October 27 investor presentation and briefing transcript, its June 30 SEC Form 17-Q, and its October 26–27 SIBOL and Citicore financing disclosures. Management’s explanations, including its account of BSP findings, remain attributed statements; the author’s stress test is illustrative, not a bank forecast.)
I welcome your views on these and other issues where decisions made in power shape the country’s economic future. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Tensions rise as US midterm campaign ends with control of Congress at stake
articles.summary: All 435 seats in the US House of Representatives and 35 of the 100 US Senate seats will be contested on November 3. Democrats are widely favored to retake the House but face a greater challenge in…

items: On the eve of the midterm elections, President Trump and congressional candidates made their final appeals to voters, with a focus on key races in Michigan and California.
Trump emphasized the importance of voter turnout in his speeches, while the Supreme Court rejected attempts by his administration to block vote counting in California.
In Michigan, Democratic candidate Abdul El-Sayed is vying to become the first Muslim elected to the Senate, facing challenges from Republicans who have questioned his loyalty.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

Congressional candidates and President Donald Trump made their final arguments to US voters on Monday, November 2, the eve of the midterm elections, with tensions running high in Michigan, where Abdul El-Sayed aims to become the first Muslim elected to the Senate.
California was also in the spotlight after the Supreme Court swiftly quashed an attempt by Trump’s Justice Department to intervene and block vote counting from alleged non-US citizens.

With control of the US Congress at stake for his final two years in office, Trump devoted his last major speech before voting day to touting renovations of the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool, one of the Washington public works projects he has made a priority since returning to the White House.
He later spoke by telephone on Fox News’ “Hannity” show, urging Republicans to pretend he is on the ballot in an effort to increase voter participation.
“We have to vote. If our people vote, we win in a landslide,” Trump said.

All 435 seats in the US House of Representatives and 35 of the 100 US Senate seats will be contested on Tuesday. Democrats are widely favored to retake the House but face a greater challenge in the Senate.

Loss of control in either chamber would constrain Trump and empower Democrats to investigate his administration, while a Senate majority would also allow them to block his appointees to federal courts including the Supreme Court.

The Supreme Court on Monday, November 2, rejected the Trump administration’s attempt to temporarily block California from counting mail-in ballots from more than 20,000 registered voters who federal officials alleged were likely non-US citizens.

It was quick action from the high court. California had argued the federal lawsuit would disenfranchise 20,000 voters based on vague accusations and that the process for identifying noncitizens was error-prone.
A US judge on Monday also ordered the Trump administration to stop demanding that California segregate ballots cast by people on lists of suspected noncitizens.

Trump, 80, has campaigned hard for Republicans, holding events in 20 states over the past 32 days, the White House said. His final in-person event was a speech at the belated reopening of the Washington reflecting pool, where the former real-estate developer spent more than 20 minutes discussing pipes, joints, caulking, granite resurfacing, algae and leaks.

“So we have a lot of great things planned for Washington, and I could get into the nation, but for that you don’t have enough time,” Trump said, also mentioning the grass at the White House, his new Marine One helipad, a golf course and plans for a triumphal arch that are facing a court challenge.
A Reuters/Ipsos poll completed on Monday found 46% of registered ​voters said they would vote for Democrats in ⁠congressional elections, compared with 38% who picked Republicans.

Early voting, whether in person or by mail, has already set a record with 57 million votes cast as of Monday afternoon, up from 45 million in all of the 2022 midterms, according to the University of Florida’s Election Lab.
In Michigan, Democratic candidate El-Sayed, a physician and former public health official, is attempting to become the first Muslim elected to the Senate, running against Republican Mike Rogers.
Their tight Senate race grew more heated over the weekend when US Representative Haley Stevens, who lost the Democratic primary to El-Sayed, switched to backing Rogers.
Afterward, El-Sayed’s campaign said it raised $2.4 million on Sunday, its largest single-day fundraising haul, fueled by small-dollar donations.

El-Sayed, an Egyptian American Muslim born in Michigan, has been targeted by Trump and other Republicans who have questioned his loyalty to the US and baselessly called him a terrorist sympathizer. El-Sayed has called questions about his loyalty to the US “shameful.”
On Fox News’ “Hannity” show on Monday Rogers cast El-Sayed as “just too extreme.”
At a Michigan rally on Monday, Rogers said, “This election was never about how someone prayed. It was always about how you think, what your philosophy and what your ideology is.”

El-Sayed appealed for unity at a campaign rally on Monday, saying, “I believe that we have the opportunity to breach those divides, divides of geography, of race, of sexual orientation, gender identity, of faith, to build together what we only can have together.”
The Trump administration also has sought to intervene in election disputes in Alaska.

A federal judge on Sunday dismissed a US Justice Department lawsuit seeking to block certification of election results in Alaska if Republican incumbent Senator Dan S. Sullivan narrowly loses. The Justice Department has argued voters may be confused by a challenger named Daniel J. Sullivan Jr. on the same ballot.

The issue of two Sullivans running in Alaska has roiled the campaign since the New York Times reported last week that Democrat Mary Peltola’s campaign was involved in recruiting the latter Sullivan into the race as a spoiler.
The senator said on Sunday he would accept the results of Tuesday’s election even as the Trump administration presses a criminal investigation into the issue.
Peltola has denied involvement, and Sullivan Jr. has denied coordinating with Peltola’s campaign.
Introduced as “the real Dan Sullivan” at a rally in Alaska on Monday, the senator said Democrats see Alaska as key to taking control of the Senate.
“It’s not just about Alaska,” he said. “We are the firewall for freedom for America right now.”

A supporter of the Senate challenger Sullivan Jr. said FBI agents on Friday questioned him about his $500 donation. Barry Bracken, a retired fisheries biologist living in Sullivan’s hometown of Petersburg, Alaska, where he said they have known each other more than 40 years, said he told the agents he had intentionally donated to Daniel J. Sullivan Jr.’s campaign, and they left soon after.
The FBI did not reply to a request for comment. – Rappler.com

articles.title: US strikes Iran ahead of midterm elections
articles.summary: US officials described the attacks on Qeshm Island as limited and defensive, according to CBS, the BBC's US partner.

blocks.text: The US has launched strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, US officials have told CBS, the BBC's US partner.
Iranian state news agency IRNA reported several explosions on the island on Monday.
The US officials described the strikes as limited and said they were in response to the Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) firing upon a US aircraft.
The BBC has contacted US Central Command (Centcom), the part of the US military responsible for operations in the Middle East, for comment.
It comes ahead of the US midterm elections, which will determine whether the Republicans or Democrats control Congress.
Trump has been facing falling polling numbers and pressure from within his party to end the war, which began when the US and Israel attacked Iran in February.
Earlier on Monday, he told reporters that he was in "no rush" to ramp up strikes on Iran.

"One way or the other, we will do something, but there is no rush. We crippled them financially," he told news outlet Axios. "They have no money, no gasoline and their people are getting very tired of it."
He also said the US "might need to go after Pickaxe", a site linked to Iran's nuclear programme, in an interview with Fox News on the eve of the midterm elections.
This was "not a big deal" and could be done in "one hour", Trump added.

There has been mounting speculation in the last few days that the US may resume significant strikes in Iran again after the midterms. But asked by a reporter on Monday if that was the case, Trump said "no".
Iran's foreign minister Abbas Araghchi told the IRNA earlier that "very intensive" talks to try and end the war are under way with the US via mediators.

He also said Tehran was prepared for both diplomatic and military scenarios "more than ever before" and that it was up to the US to choose between a "wise path" of negotiation or the "mistake of military aggression".

Peel police say a situation at the University of Toronto Mississauga campus is "contained" after students were told to shelter in place due to an "active incident" Monday night.

There is a large police presence in the area of Mississauga Road and Outer Circle Road at the university and people are urged to avoid the area, police said in a post on X.

The UTM said it had received reports of police activity at Mcluhan Court residence, 3330 Residence Road.

articles.title: Supreme Court rejects Trump's request to stop California counting disputed votes
articles.summary: The ruling, which comes on the eve of the midterm elections, essentially ends the Trump administration's bid to disqualify the ballots in the state.

blocks.text: Image source, Getty Images
BySareen Habeshian
Reporting fromLos Angeles
The US Supreme Court has rejected a last-minute request by the Trump administration asking it to intervene in California's midterm election vote count.
The justice department wanted 20,000 ballots to be set aside that it alleged may have been issued to non-US citizens in the state.
Two lower courts had already rejected the request. State election officials had questioned the federal government's claims - saying the process used to identify alleged non-citizens was inaccurate.
The Monday ruling comes on the eve of the midterms, which will determine which political party controls the US Congress for the last two years of President Donald Trump's second term.
The Supreme Court announced its decision in a one-line order, saying it was denying the justice department's request for an injunction.
"The application for injunction pending appeal presented to Justice Kagan and by her referred to the Court is denied," it reads.
Its means rulings made in lower courts will stand and essentially ends the Trump administration's bid to disqualify the ballots.

California is the most populous state in America with some 23 million people on its voting register. As of Sunday night, more than six million mail-in ballots had already been received, according to the California secretary of state's office.

The justice department sent letters to the California secretary of state and Los Angeles County Registrar last month, demanding they set aside the ballots of 20,000 registered voters whom the Trump administration "believe" are "likely" non-citizens, according to court documents.

About a week later, armed officials from the Department of Homeland Security delivered letters to county officials and employees across California threatening criminal charges if they didn't sequester those ballots.
In a 22-page brief reviewed by the BBC, the justice department maintained that ballots cast by non-citizens could "debase or dilute valid votes".
On Friday, a federal appeals court declined the government's request to segregate the ballots.
California election officials have questioned the accuracy of the government's claims, and have said the list of names the government has provided is riddled with inaccuracies.
They have expressed concern that eligible voters could be disenfranchised and said segregating ballots whilst voting is underway is unfeasible.
What are Americans voting for this election?
The attempts are a part of a years-long campaign by Trump and his administration to fight alleged voter fraud that they believe is widespread, despite research showing that it is extremely rare.

President Trump has repeatedly claimed that Democrats steal elections by allowing immigrants to vote illegally, and he blames much of it on the so-called "mail-in" or postal voting that is permitted in many Democratic states.

Last week in a scathing ruling, district judge David Carter said the government's move in California was indicative of an "ongoing pattern of attempted election interference" on the part of the Trump administration.

The judge added that "never before in American history has the federal government, on the eve of an election, sought to coerce a state and local government to abandon their own constitutional elections procedures and bend to the will of the executive branch".
With additional reporting by the BBC's David Willis

articles.title: RBA interest rates: Reserve Bank hikes cash rate for fifth time this year in blow to mortgage holders
articles.summary: Reserve Bank of Australia increases official cash rate to 4.85%, bringing it to highest level since 2008

blocks.text: The Reserve Bank has hiked rates for the fifth time this year, from 4.6% to 4.85%, in an attempt to regain control of surging inflation amid an ongoing global oil shock triggered by the war in the Middle East.

The RBA’s decision to hit mortgage holders again is no surprise after inflation jumped to 4.3% in the year to September and comes following tough talk from senior central bank officials over recent days and weeks.
The decision split the monetary policy board, with six members voting for a hike, while three were in favour of holding the cash rate steady.
In its post-meeting statement following the decision, the board repeated that it “will continue to do what it considers necessary to bring inflation sustainably back to target”.
The statement did not include an explicit reference to the potential need for further hikes, signalling the RBA is now prepared to wait and see the effects of this year’s five rate rises.
The cash rate has reached its highest level since 2008.
Back-to-back hikes will heap more pain on over 3.3m households with home loans and turn the screws on a federal government under pressure for its economic management.
The latest rate rise will lift the monthly interest payment on a $700,000 home loan by $107, according to Canstar, bringing the total rise in repayments over this year’s five hikes to $532.

As the central bank struggles to explain to Australians how interest rate hikes will help tame inflation fueled by events overseas, the RBA’s latest set of forecasts in its Statement on Monetary Policy (SOMP) showed a difficult period ahead for the economy.
The forecasts showed the country’s cost of living crisis would extend for another year, even as Australia struggles with below trend economic growth and climbing unemployment.

The 4.3% inflation rate in the year to September was substantially stronger than the RBA had anticipated as a worsening Middle East conflict squashed hopes of a quick resolution to the global oil shock.

Inflation will push higher through the final months of 2026 and only return below 3% – within the bank’s 2-3% target range – by the end of next year, or about nine months later than hoped, the latest forecasts showed.

Amid a heated political stoush over whether the federal government’s spending is to blame for high and rising inflation, the RBA noted in its SOMP that public demand was weaker than expected through the first six months of 2026.
That was the result of cost of living measures rolling off and “moderating” spending in areas such as defence and disability and aged care services, the SOMP said.

Global oil prices would ease over the coming 18 months, but still remain relatively elevated, according to the forecasts, suggesting limited relief from high fuel costs for motorists and ongoing high costs for businesses.
“We view the risks to the inflation outlook as still skewed to the upside,” the report said.
Alongside persistent cost of living pressures, the RBA also predicted weak economic growth through to the end of 2028.
The economy would grow by 1.6% this year and by 1.3% in 2027.
That would be well below an estimated potential growth rate of around 2%, but better than recent forecasts by bank analysts.

And despite the risks associated with a housing downturn that “is one of the steepest over the past 50 years”, the central banks’ economists saw no evidence that the country was headed towards recession over the coming two years.
Unemployment, now at 4.7%, would end next year at around 4.9%, before creeping over 5% in 2028. Importantly, employment would remain positive.
Meanwhile, there was no end in sight for the global artificial intelligence boom, which would continue to add to capacity issues in Australia.
The RBA nearly tripled its forecast for business investment growth in 2026 to 12%.

articles.title: US reportedly strikes Iran’s Qeshm Island as Vance voices optimism about a deal
articles.summary:
Iranian state media reported the sound of explosions on the island in the strait of Hormuz, coming on the eve of crucial US midterms

The ⁠US launched limited strikes on ​Iran’s Qeshm Island…

blocks.text: The ⁠US launched limited strikes on ​Iran’s Qeshm Island late on Monday, ⁠according to reports in US media, hours after US vice-president JD Vance said he was optimistic diplomatic efforts to end the war were moving in the right direction.

The strikes were reported as being “defensive”, and not thought to be a signal of a return to full hostilities, but came on the eve of crucial midterm elections in which Donald Trump’s Republican party is expected to be punished by voters for the cascading effect the war has had on the US cost of living.
When asked earlier on Monday whether he had considered resuming strikes on Iran after Tuesday’s midterm elections, Trump replied “no”.

Several explosions were ⁠heard ⁠on Qeshm ​Island on Monday evening, according to Iranian state media, with local outlets describing their cause as unclear. The strikes – first reported by the Wall Street Journal (WSJ) – targeted surface to air missiles being used against US assets, according to Reuters and the Associated Press.

US Central ‌Command did ​not immediately ⁠respond to ​a request for ​comment from the Reuters news agency, and the WSJ described the attacks as part of a series of strikes carried out against the country in recent weeks that have not been made public.

The paper said that sources suggested the recent strikes have been carried out on a smaller scale and purposefully kept secret by the Trump administration so as not to signal ‌any intent of resuming the military campaign against Iran.

The US has targeted Qeshm Island on multiple occasions throughout the war. Positioned in the mouth of the strait of Hormuz, the island has been used in the past to launch attacks on shipping in the waterway.

Despite attacks having ceased in recent weeks, Iran has continued to enforce its closure of the strait by targeting oil tankers, shipping containers and other vessels attempting to transit the waterway.

If confirmed, the attack would mark the first publicly known strike by the US on Iran in weeks. On Monday Vance said that he and Trump were optimistic about securing a deal with Iran, after Tehran revealed indirect negotiations with Washington.

“The president and I both feel pretty good about the prospects for potentially coming to a negotiated settlement,” Vance told reporters. “We’ve certainly made some progress. We’ll see if we can make some more.”
Speaking to Fox News hours before the polls opened in the US on Tuesday, Trump continued to play down the significance of the conflict and its effects on the US economy.
“There’s no war raging. It could happen if they don’t make a deal, but they want to make a deal very badly and there’s a very good chance we make a deal.”

Speaking from Washington in his closing message of the midterms campaign, Trump hailed a sharp drop in oil prices that came as his administration touted a renewed diplomatic efforts being made to end the war. Rising petrol prices have caused by the war have become a signature issue of the midterm elections, with polls showing voters likely to punish Republicans for the effect on the cost of living.

articles.title: Tennessee national guard trained guns on dying man after guard member shot him, video shows
articles.summary:
Footage from prosecutors shows aftermath of shooting of Tyrin Johnson, 20, shot and killed by national guard in July

Tennessee national guard troops in Memphis last summer trained their…

blocks.text: Tennessee national guard troops in Memphis last summer trained their handguns on a man as he lay dying on a sidewalk after a guard member shot him in the back, video released Monday by county prosecutors shows.
A Memphis police officer can be heard in the footage from an officer’s body camera calling for an ambulance and then asking the troops: “Hey, you guys got a medical kit or anything?”

The Shelby county district attorney’s office released the videos, which also include footage from stationary cameras and a cellphone from a bystander, as the Tennessee Bureau of Investigation continues its investigation into the 5 July shooting of Tyrin Johnson.

Johnson, 20, who had been armed, died at the scene from a single gunshot wound, according to investigators. An autopsy report shared by Johnson’s family found that he was shot in the back, contradicting police and national guard accounts that said he was facing the guard members with a gun when they fired at him.
The footage did not show Johnson’s initial encounter with the guard members or them firing at him.

The guard members were part of a federal taskforce created by Donald Trump, who last year sent troops and federal agents to Democratic-run cities that he described as overrun with crime. Tennessee’s Republican governor Bill Lee had deployed the guard to support the effort. The task force was involved in four fatal shootings between May and July.
District attorney Steve Mulroy said he has not yet decided whether to file charges in connection with the death.

A spokesperson for the Tennessee national guard did not immediately respond to email and phone messages seeking comment. Ed Yarbrough, an attorney for the two guard members, said they have no comment at this time.
Authorities said the troops were responding with local police to reports of gunshots at about 4am when they began pursuing an armed man fleeing on foot.

Footage from stationary street cameras shows a person in dark clothing firing shots through an empty parking lot at three people walking on a sidewalk. Two Memphis police officers hear gunshots nearby and start walking and then running in that direction, a body camera worn by one of the officers shows. The officers say on their radio that they are pursuing a man who is running and armed with a gun.
The video, which is blurry from the officer’s movement, captures yelling and the sound of a single gunshot, followed by several additional gunshot noises.

A Tennessee national guard report obtained by the Associated Press via a public records request said two guard members responded to the Memphis police radio call, left their vehicle and approached the suspect, who “rounded on them and pointed a tan handgun at them”. Both guard members fired their service weapons – M17 handguns – and Memphis police arrived shortly after, the report stated.
Police body camera footage shows guard members at the scene shouting “Hands!” and “Turn over!” as they point their handguns at a man lying on his back on the sidewalk.
André C Wharton, an attorney for Johnson’s family, noted that the videos do not show the moments immediately before the shooting, or the shooting itself.
“This investigation must stay focused on the moment the guardsman fired the fatal shot and whether that action was reasonable,” Wharton said.
Johnson was the father of a young child and was preparing to help lead the family construction business, his grandfather, Evaniel Johnson, said.

At least six guard members were on the scene immediately after the shooting, the body camera video shows. One can be seen moving a handgun that is on the ground until a police officer tells him to leave it alone. An officer calls for an ambulance over the radio, and a guard member begins to cut off the man’s shirt just before the video ends.

articles.title: DepEd procures over 170,000 Macbooks for teachers, staff
articles.summary: The Department of Education has purchased 170,000 Apple MacBook Neo laptops, in what Apple's chief executive called the company's biggest education deal ever for the Mac.

blocks.text: November 3, 2026 | 10:51am
MANILA, Philippines (Second update, 12:48 p.m.) — The Department of Education has bought 172,654 Apple MacBook Neo laptops for public school teachers and administrative staff at about P43,000 each.

DepEd said on Tuesday, November 3, it had concluded competitive bidding for the laptops. Of the total, 169,008 will go to teachers and 3,646 to administrative officers. Deliveries are scheduled from this month through March 2027.

"For the longest time, our teachers have carried the heavy personal burden of buying their own laptops or maintaining outdated equipment just to keep up with lesson plans," Education Secretary Sonny Angara said in a statement. "Under the vision of President Marcos, we are changing the narrative."
The MacBooks bring the number of teacher laptops DepEd has contracted so far under its computerization program to 231,725, including 62,717 Windows-based units.
That is enough for roughly one in four of the country's nearly 900,000 public school teachers.

President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. has pledged that every public school teacher will have a laptop before his term ends in 2028, and DepEd had planned to buy more than 250,000 laptops for teaching personnel under its 2026 budget.

The pace of the program has drawn criticism, particularly from the teachers' group the Alliance of Concerned Teachers (ACT). In a statement in August, the group faulted DepEd for handing out voice amplifiers while teachers were still waiting for their own laptops, and said the planned 250,000 units would still leave most teachers without one.
At the time, DepEd replied that the laptop purchase was taking longer because the devices had to meet standards for performance, durability, battery life and warranty.
Price and warranty
DepEd said the P43,000 price covers the laptop, built-in productivity software, delivery and teacher training, and is about P6,900 below the base model's suggested retail price.
At that price, the order is worth about P7.4 billion. The department did not disclose the exact contract amount.
The five-year warranty on the MacBook Neos is a first for DepEd's laptop purchases, the department said. Retail units carry one year of coverage.
The unit price is about P15,300 lower than what DepEd paid in 2021, when the procurement service of the Department of Budget and Management bought 39,583 laptops for teachers at P58,300 each.
The Commission on Audit later flagged that P2.4-billion purchase as overpriced given the laptops ran on outdated processors.
Apple's biggest Mac education deal
Apple chief executive John Ternus shared the deal during the company's fourth-quarter earnings call early Tuesday, Manila time, his first since he succeeded Tim Cook in September.

"I'm feeling great about the opportunities ahead for Apple, from our product roadmap and broad range of services to promising areas like health, emerging markets, enterprise and education," Ternus said. "As one example, we recently secured our biggest education deal ever for Mac with the Department of Education in the Philippines. They're going to deploy 170,000 MacBook Neos to teachers and staff."
"Opportunities like this bring more users into our ecosystem and help fuel growth across our business," he added.
Apple launched the MacBook Neo in March as its cheapest laptop. It runs on the A18 Pro, a chip first used in iPhones.
It also raised the laptop's Philippine retail price by P10,000 in June amid a global shortage of memory chips.
Apple also told analysts that Mac supplies would remain constrained through the October-to-December quarter, when DepEd's first deliveries are due.

articles.title: Man and boy arrested after allegedly attacking One Nation volunteer with baseball bat in Australia
articles.summary: The incident comes amid growing calls for the temperature of political debate in Australia to be turned down.

blocks.text: Two people have been arrested after a volunteer for Australia's right-wing populist party One Nation was allegedly assaulted with a baseball bat.
A man, 37, and a boy, 14, were arrested on Sunday night after an incident outside the volunteer's home in Torquay, about 100km (62 miles) south-west of Melbourne.
The man was charged with assault offences and remanded in custody while the boy was issued with a caution. The volunteer was hospitalised with non-life threatening injuries, police said.
One Nation's Victorian leader Warren Pickering claimed the attack happened after the pair "interfered with" election signs on the volunteer's property.
Pickering said the alleged assault was "un-Australian and unacceptable".
"Political violence or intimidation of any kind against anyone is unacceptable in this country," he said.
"If you don't like someone's politics, you vote accordingly. You don't assault them."
Victorian Premier Ben Carroll described the attack as "shocking".
"Whether you're wearing a red, a blue, an orange, or a green T-shirt, they are volunteers," he said.
"They are out there doing what they believe is right, and no one should be coming under attack."

The alleged attack comes during a state election campaign in Victoria, and amid a reckoning in the country more broadly over the tone of political debate, after the attack on Federal MP Helen Haines last month.

Police have not detailed a motive for the incident - which left Haines needing both of her legs amputated - but politicians, law enforcement, and experts have said heated public discourse is heightening the threat of political violence in the country.

articles.title: US Supreme Court rejects Trump, lets California count all ballots
articles.summary: The decision represents another defeat for Trump as his fellow Republicans fight to retain control of Congress in the November 3 midterms. California is the most populous US state and a Democratic…

blocks.text: INJUNCTION ORDER. A US judge blocks an order to detain British national Imran Ahmed, CEO of the Center for Countering Digital Hate
Dado Ruvic/Reuters

The decision represents another defeat for Trump as his fellow Republicans fight to retain control of Congress in the November 3 midterms. California is the most populous US state and a Democratic stronghold.

items: The Supreme Court rejected the Trump administration's request to block California from counting mail-in ballots from over 20,000 registered voters alleged to be non-US citizens, allowing the state to proceed with its elections.

California Governor Gavin Newsom welcomed the decision, asserting that it ensures a free and fair election, while the administration's claims of widespread noncitizen voting have been widely discredited.

The case highlighted constitutional tensions between state and federal election administration, with a federal judge criticizing the administration's attempt to influence state election procedures on the eve of the midterms.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

Acting on the eve of the US midterm elections, the Supreme Court quickly rejected on Monday, November 2, a bid by President Donald Trump‘s administration to temporarily block California from counting mail-in ballots from more than 20,000 registered voters who federal officials allege are likely non-US citizens.

The justices denied the Justice Department’s emergency request just hours after it filed it, shutting down the administration’s claims over disputed ballots that could have affected thousands of voters and injected uncertainty into election outcomes.

The decision represented another defeat for Trump as his fellow Republicans fight to retain control of Congress in Tuesday’s midterms. California is the most populous US state and a Democratic stronghold.
The administration intensified its focus on alleged noncitizen voting in the run-up to the midterms. Multiple studies and state audits show that ineligible voting, including by noncitizens, is rare.

blocks.caption: Three issues defining the 2026 US midterm elections

blocks.text: The Supreme Court’s brief, one-sentence order on Monday did not offer any explanation of its action, as is common when it handles emergency matters. No justice publicly dissented from the decision. The court also did not ask California for a response to the administration’s request, a step that, when taken, usually signals serious consideration of an emergency case.
California Governor Gavin Newsom, a Democrat, called the decision “a welcome sight for all Americans given the disgusting and dangerous attacks on our democracy by the federal government.”
“Tomorrow (Tuesday), Californians can feel secure in knowing the state will carry out a free and fair election — just as we’ve always done,” Newsom added.
A federal appeals court refused the administration’s request on Friday.
The administration had demanded that California separate any allegedly unlawful ballots from other ballots and not count them until those voters are determined to be US citizens.
“Once California commingles the challenged ballots with lawful ones, there is no way to get the challenged ballots back,” the Justice Department said in its request to the Supreme Court.
Trump has made false claims about widespread US voting fraud including in the 2020 election lost to Democrat Joe Biden.

“We will continue pursuing every available legal avenue to protect the integrity of our elections and ensure federal law is enforced,” acting US Deputy Attorney General Trent ​McCotter said in a social media post after the administration’s filing earlier in the day.

The US Constitution assigns the responsibility of administering elections to states, though the federal government has some oversight. The lawsuit marked a rare federal intervention in the voting process and signaled a willingness by the administration to contest the election results in court.

The administration already sought to restrict voting by mail — a mode of casting ballots used more often by Democratic-leaning voters — but the Supreme Court in September rebuffed that effort. And a federal judge on Sunday dismissed the administration’s lawsuit concerning the US Senate race in Alaska.
The list of 20,000 registered voters was amassed by the US Department of Homeland Security and sent to California officials and to Los Angeles County officials.

The Justice Department sued in federal court on October 15, claiming California is unlawfully preventing its enforcement of a 1996 US law that makes it a criminal offense for noncitizens to vote in federal elections. The department said California’s action violated the Constitution’s Supremacy Clause, which holds that federal law generally preempts state law.

California has said that the state’s safeguards against noncitizen voting are robust and that the lawsuit threatens to deprive 20,000 people of their right to vote based on vague accusations. The administration’s process for scrutinizing voter lists to identify noncitizens is flawed and likely rife with errors, it said in court papers.
California has 52 seats in the House of Representatives, more than any other state. Democrats need a net gain of four House seats to win a majority in the chamber.
US District Judge David Carter in Los Angeles denied the administration’s request on October 28.

“Never before in American history has the federal government, on the eve of an election, sought to coerce a state and local government to abandon their own constitutional elections procedures and bend to the will of the executive branch,” Carter wrote.

blocks.caption: What you need to know about the 2026 US midterm elections

blocks.text: Carter raised concerns over the reliability of the administration’s data, noting that people recently flagged by the federal government as noncitizens on voter rolls in other states have repeatedly turned out to be naturalized US citizens.
“If the executive can discount votes and threaten an ongoing election due to unproven allegations, then our democracy is in danger,” Carter wrote.

The San Francisco-based 9th US Circuit Court of Appeals also refused on Friday to block the ballots, emphasizing the state’s power over election procedures and California’s “comprehensive statutory scheme to ensure the integrity of its elections,” including a system for canceling registrations if a voter is shown to be ineligible. – Rappler.com

articles.title: North Korea denies being behind record $6.3bn Binance hack
articles.summary: US government agencies and cyber analysts have blamed Pyongyang for the record-breaking heist.

blocks.text: North Korea has denied claims that it was behind the record $6.3bn (£4.7bn) hack of cryptocurrency exchange Binance, calling the allegations an "absurd rhetoric".

Kim Yo-jong, a top Democratic People's Republic of Korea official and the sister of leader Kim Jong Un, said on Tuesday that the accusations are another "sinister attempt" by the US to damage the country's public image.
The US Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), the Secret Service and cyber analysts have said North Korea orchestrated the hack - which has been described as the largest in history.
Pyongyang has also been blamed for a number of major cyber attacks - accusations that it has consistently denied.
Blockchain analysts and the FBI have said the attack was led by state-backed hacking group TraderTraitor.
The FBI has called on industry partners to help block transactions involving cryptocurrency accounts linked to the group.
"The US has made a trite provocation of linking it with the Democratic People's Republic of Korea again," Kim Yo-jong, the director of North Korea's General Affairs Department, said in a statement.
"It is a grave political provocation against the DPRK that the US misleads the international public opinion as if all the cyber crimes in different parts of the world are our deeds," she said.
The incident is the latest hack to be linked to North Korea, which has been accused of relying on cyber-crime to help finance its economy.
The TraderTraitor unit, which is also known as the Lazarus Group, was blamed for a then-record $1.5bn hack of crypto exchange Bybit in 2025.

Pyongyang has systematically built its cyber operations, recruiting promising students from universities and sending them to hacker units overseen by North Korea's intelligence agency, research groups like the S Rajaratnam School of International Studies think tank have said.
The country has consistently denied such claims.
Kim Yo-jong said "it is the consistent policy stand of the DPRK government to resolutely oppose all sorts of malicious acts in cyberspace".
The BBC has contacted Binance for comment. Since the hack, the crypto giant has largely focused its public statements on the technical nature of the breach and its response to protect users.
The company said initial checks indicated that an engineer's laptop had been compromised, enabling an attacker to make unauthorised withdrawals.
Trading in major cryptocurrencies on Binance has since resumed after the exchange worked with issuers to freeze assets impacted by the hack.
Binance said on Sunday that its customers pulled out more than $3.6bn of assets from its exchange as it reopened after suspending all transactions in the wake of the hack.
The company has repeatedly said it would cover all of the losses linked to the attack and that it has so far covered around 95% of the assets stolen in the breach.

articles.title: Russian bombing of Ukrainian aid centre kills at least 26, Kyiv says
articles.summary:
Ukrainian president Zelenskyy says attack on aid hub was ‘vile’ and shows Russia does not want to de-escalate

Russia on Monday bombed an aid distribution centre and neighbouring shelter in…

blocks.text: Russia on Monday bombed an aid distribution centre and neighbouring shelter in southern Ukraine, killing at least 26 ​people, Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy and the country’s emergency services said.

Emergency services said two members of a rescue crew and four police officers were among the dead in the village ⁠of Komyshuvakha, in south-eastern Zaporizhzhia region. Five people were being treated in hospital, including two rescue workers.
Zelenskyy, in his nightly video address, said Russian forces initially dropped bombs on a school in the village that was used as a shelter and for ⁠distributing humanitarian assistance.
There were no classes at the school, he said, as the village, lying south-east of the region’s main city, ​also called Zaporizhzhia, was too close to the frontline. ‌
“The Russians struck first ‌just as people were arriving – a few aerial bombs,” he said. “Then there was a second strike – more air bombs, this time on ‌the shelter. A vile terrorist strike.”

As night fell in Komyshuvakha, emergency responders used torches to search through the rubble of collapsed buildings, according to photos and video posted online by local officials. Regina Kharchenko, secretary of the Zaporizhzhia city council, said that 27 people were missing in the attack.

Efforts to rescue people Monday evening were hindered as Russian drones launched additional attacks in the area that had been bombed, according to Mykhailo Semikin, a military official in Zaporizhzhia.
Zelenskyy said the Russians could not have been unaware that residents remaining in Komyshuvakha gathered each week to pick up humanitarian packages from the site.

blocks.caption: Ukrainian soldiers stand among the rubble after a Russian airstrike on the humanitarian aid hub. Photograph: Reuters

blocks.text: The attack, he said, had shown that Moscow was intent on killing people instead of building on the past week’s ceasefire in the embattled southern city of Oleshky, brokered by US first lady Melania Trump.
“Russians continue to demonstrate, time and again, their hatred of Ukraine and everything that exists here,” he said.
“If Russia genuinely ‌wanted de-escalation, there was an opportunity following the situation in Oleshky to continue taking humanitarian steps. We proposed this. But Russia continues to kill people.”
The ceasefire last week enabled an evacuation of the Russian-occupied Oleshky.
It was the longest pause in fighting between the neighbours in the war, now in its fifth year, which has killed hundreds of thousands of people and displaced millions.
The Kremlin said that no other similar missions were being planned “at the moment”.
US-led talks between Russia and Ukraine are set to resume next week, US special envoy Steve Witkoff said on Monday.
President Donald Trump has pushed for a settlement to the dragging war but there has been no breakthrough.
The talks – to be held 10 November and 11 in Abu Dhabi, Witkoff said – come as Kyiv and its European allies worry that Trump has increasingly sided with Moscow.
*With Reuters, Associated Press and Agence France-Presse

A man showers with a hose during hot weather in Manila on April 28, 2024.
AFP / Earvin Perias

MANILA, Philippines — State weather bureau PAGASA warned of dangerous heat conditions in 16 areas across the country on Tuesday, November 3, with the heat index expected to peak at 43 degrees Celsius.
Iloilo City, San Jose in Occidental Mindoro and Catarman in Northern Samar are expected to record the highest heat index at 43°C.
Heat index refers to the temperature felt by the human body when relative humidity combines with actual air temperature.
Under PAGASA’s classification, “danger” levels range from 42°C to 51°C. Prolonged exposure to these conditions may cause heat cramps and heat exhaustion and could lead to heat stroke.

blocks.text: What to do under extreme heat
Amid soaring temperatures, the public is advised to take the following precautions to avoid heat-related illnesses:

items: Avoid prolonged exposure to direct sunlight, especially during the hottest hours of the day.
Stay in shaded or well-ventilated areas whenever possible.
Wear lightweight and loose-fitting clothing.
Drink plenty of water to stay hydrated.
Use umbrellas, hats or caps when outdoors.
Watch for symptoms of heat-related illnesses, including headaches, vomiting and muscle cramps. Seek medical attention if symptoms worsen.

articles.title: PDP-Laban holds indignation rally outside SC for Rodrigo Duterte, Bato dela Rosa
articles.summary: Despite rainy weather, members and supporters of political party Partido Demokratiko Pilipino-Lakas ng Bayan (PDP-Laban) gathered outside the Supreme Court (SC) on Tuesday morning.

blocks.text: Published November 3, 2026 8:58am
Despite rainy weather, members and supporters of political party Partido Demokratiko Pilipino-Lakas ng Bayan (PDP-Laban) gathered outside the Supreme Court (SC) on Tuesday morning.
The group held an indignation rally calling for the swift resolution of cases involving former President Rodrigo Duterte and Senator Ronald "Bato” dela Rosa.
“Hindi alintana ang ulan, patuloy ang pagdating at pagtitipon ng mga kababayan natin sa harap ng Korte Suprema ngayong Martes ng umaga, November 3, para sa isang Indignation Rally,” PDP-Laban said.
(Despite the rain, our countrymen continue to arrive and gather in front of the Supreme Court this Tuesday morning, November 3, for an Indignation Rally.)
“Sa kabila ng masamang panahon, tuloy ang pagpapahayag ng kanilang paninindigan” it added.
(Despite the bad weather, they continue to express their stance.
PDP-Laban is set to submit a letter to the SC reiterating its appeal for an immediate ruling on the cases.
'Delays'

In an open letter issued on October 31 and signed by acting chairman Alfonso Cusi, the political party urged the SC to resolve the legal questions surrounding Duterte and Dela Rosa, saying prolonged delays could further fuel uncertainty and instability.
PDP-Laban questioned the alleged procedural delays in the cases, noting that a habeas corpus petition filed on behalf of Duterte had remained pending before the high tribunal for nearly 600 days.
It also called for the immediate resolution of Dela Rosa's pending motion for reconsideration.
Duterte was arrested by Philippine authorities in Pasay City and was handed over to the International Criminal Court (ICC) on March 11, 2025.

He was flown via a chartered plane to The Hague, where he will be tried for crimes against humanity in relation to his bloody war on drugs while he was mayor of Davao City and President of the Philippines.
The trial is scheduled to begin on November 30, 2026.
Dela Rosa is also wanted by the ICC as he is accused of being a co-perpetrator in the alleged crimes.
A P50-million reward is being offered for information that would lead to the senator’s arrest. —VAL, GMA News

articles.title: Man and boy arrested after One Nation volunteer allegedly attacked with baseball bat in Victoria
articles.summary:
Police confirm arrest of 37-year-old and 14-year-old boy over alleged assault outside Torquay home on Sunday night

A man and boy have been arrested after a One Nation volunteer was allegedly…

blocks.text: A man and boy have been arrested after a One Nation volunteer was allegedly attacked with a baseball bat outside his home on Victoria’s Surf Coast.
Police on Tuesday confirmed they arrested a 37-year-old Hampton park man and a 14-year-old boy over the incident, which occurred at a Torquay home on Sunday night.
“Investigators have been told the males allegedly assaulted the victim at a premises on Scorpio Street about 7.45pm,” a police spokesperson said.
“It is believed they allegedly assaulted the man with a baseball bat before being arrested by attending units a short time later.”
The victim – a 60-year-old man – was taken to hospital with non-life threatening injuries.
One Nation’s federal leader, Pauline Hanson, and Victorian deputy leader, Colleen Harkin, were expected to visit the man in hospital on Tuesday morning.
The Hampton Park man was charged with intentionally causing injury and other assault-related offences was remanded in custody appear again on 10 November.
The boy was issued with a caution.
One Nation’s Victorian leader, Warren Pickering, said the alleged attack was on a party volunteer and described it as “un-Australian and unacceptable.”
He alleged the incident began when the man and the boy “interfered with” the One Nation signs on the man’s property .
“Political violence or intimidation of any kinda against anyone is unacceptable in this country,” Pickering said.
“If you don’t like someone’s politics, you vote accordingly. You don’t [allegedly] assault them.”
It comes as police are also searching for a woman as part of its investigation into an incident involving Liberal party MP Georgie Crozier last month.

Police on Tuesday morning said the 62-year-old was handing out flyers with a group of volunteers outside a supermarket on Bay Street in Port Melbourne on 17 October when she was approached by an unknown woman who appeared substance affected.
A short time later, a vehicle mounted a gutter near the group, before it swerved toward nearby traffic lights and left the scene.
Police said those involved where “shaken” following the incident but not physically injured.
They have released an image of a woman they hope will be able to assist their investigation and are calling for any other witnesses to come forward.
MPs in Victoria are on high alert in the lead up to the 28 November state election, following the alleged attack on the federal MP Helen Haines last month.

Last week, Victoria’s emergency services minister, Paul Edbrooke, told reporters he believed he was being followed and feared for his family’s safety after a bullet, etched with the word “RAT” and his former firefighter number, was left on his car.
Animal Justice Party MP Georgie Purcell and Nationals MP Annabelle Cleeland have also raised concerns about threats.
More details soon …
